text:
Shane Wright has a new team and, six games in, a fresh start. The fourth pick in 2022 came to Nashville from Seattle this month, and on Nov. 11 in Anaheim he had his first goal as a Predator plus two assists, in what was the team's sixth straight win. Heavy.com and CBS Sports both marked the moment; for a 22-year-old who carried "No. 1 prospect" expectations into the league, it matters.

His season line is modest: seven points in 20 games, 14 minutes a night, no power-play points. But the numbers under it are steady. He's shooting 12.9%, right on his norm, and his chance rate (0.95 individual expected goals per 60) is up from last season. His team has scored a few more goals than expected with him on, so the points aren't hiding.

The case for him has always been the details. Evolving-Hockey had most of his 1.3 wins above replacement last season coming from even-strength defense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 65% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. What we'd watch in Nashville is role: whether 14 minutes becomes 17.
